args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks immediately after the v2.3.1 production deploy, with error rate spiking to 18% across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. In response, the service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent version previously healthy in production. Post-rollback verification confirms checkout-api is healthy again on v2.3.0 with error rate at 0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation; note v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the prod rollout, suggesting insufficient gating.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Summary of actions:

1. **Diagnosed**: v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rolled back**: checkout-api rolled back to **v2.3.0** (the most recent healthy production release) in all regions.
3. **Verified**: Service is now healthy on v2.3.0, error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Incident opened**: **INC-0001** (SEV2) titled "checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0", with a summary of the failure and remediation. On-call has been paged.

One thing worth flagging to the on-call team: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before the production rollout, so the staging gating for this release may need review alongside the root-cause investigation of v2.3.1.
